title: Select Revelations of S. Mechtild
author: Mechthild of Magdeburg
description: Select Revelations of S. Mechtild, Virgin, taken from the five books of her Spiritual Grace and translated from the Latin by 'a secular priest' (London: T. Richardson, 1875), a selection from the Liber specialis gratiae (Book of Special Grace). Although the library index lists Mechthild of Magdeburg, the text, which speaks of 'Blessed Mechtild' and her 'praiseworthy conversation' as recorded by companions, matches the visionary record of St Mechtild of Hackeborn (1241-1298), the Cistercian-Benedictine nun of Helfta and mistress of the choir, compiled largely by her sister nun St Gertrude the Great. The selected revelations are bound up with the liturgy of the Divine Office and the Mass and develop an affective, Christ-centred mysticism of the Sacred Heart, communion of saints and intercession for souls. The Helfta convent was an exceptional centre of women's mysticism in the thirteenth century, and Mechtild's book was widely read in late medieval Europe.
